text:
Are you curious about the future of technology and how it will impact our world? Join the University of Rhode Island as they celebrate World Quantum Day , coinciding with the International Year of Quantum, providing a deep dive into the exciting world of quantum science. this event highlights URI’s advancements in quantum details science and its innovative interdisciplinary programs, offering valuable insights into this rapidly evolving field.
University Of Rhode Island Celebrates World Quantum Day Amidst International Year Of Quantum Kingston, R.I. – April 9, 2025
The University of Rhode Island’s physics department is set to host its fourth annual World Quantum Day, coinciding with the United Nations’ declaration of 2025 as the International year of Quantum.This event highlights URI’s growing quantum information science programs and interdisciplinary initiatives.
URI’s Quantum Day: A Deep Dive Into Quantum Science The University of Rhode Island (URI) is gearing up to celebrate World Quantum Day on friday, April 11 , from noon to 6 p.m. on the Kingston campus. This annual event, organized by the URI physics department , aims to boost public awareness and understanding of quantum science and technology.
Event Highlights: Remarks from U.S. Sen. Jack reed (pre-recorded). Talk by Tina Brower-Thomas, co-principal investigator, National Science Foundation-funded Center for Integrated Quantum Materials at Howard. Keynote address by Suhail Zubairy, Texas A&M University. Discussion groups for students and alumni. 2025: A Year Dedicated To Quantum Mechanics The United Nations has declared 2025 as the International Year of Quantum, marking the centennial of quantum mechanics. This milestone celebrates the groundbreaking theories of 1925 that demonstrated quantum mechanics’ potential to solve problems beyond the scope of classical mechanics.
Today,as we enter what’s being called the second revolution of quantum,scientists are leveraging quantum mechanics in diverse fields,including computation,measurement,and interaction. Quantum communication, as a notable example, enables the rapid and secure transmission of encrypted messages, effectively preventing eavesdropping.
URI’s Quantum Information Science Programs Thrive Quantum information science is experiencing meaningful growth within URI’s College of Arts and Sciences. The university offers both a master’s degree and an online graduate certificate program in quantum computing . These programs have collectively secured nearly $3 million in federal funding, including two National Science Foundation grants awarded last fall to bolster quantum research. Furthermore, the department is developing a quantum computing track for undergraduate students.
Bridging The Gap: Quantum Physics And The Humanities Leonard Kahn, professor and department chair, emphasizes the importance of these developments, stating, All of this is so positive. We want to bring attention to what the physics department is doing and how the College of Arts and Sciences has supported us.
Kahn is collaborating with Thomas Stubblefield, the college’s associate dean, to establish a campus quantum humanities network. Inspired by Universität Innsbruck in Austria, this initiative aims to foster interdisciplinary collaboration between STEM fields and the humanities.The goal is to leverage expertise from the humanities and social sciences to inform the request of quantum physics and promote a deeper understanding of its societal implications.
That network aims to use interdisciplinary collaboration and expertise in the humanities and social sciences to inform the use of quantum physics in these fields and contribute to a better understanding of its consequences.
According to Kahn, This is what makes the work worthwhile; we’re making a difference in the college.
For more information about URI’s World Quantum Day, visit https://physics.uri.edu/2025wqd/
